{"id":"mimid-1wgh.37.90.18","title":"wg: virtual-clients-01 L623 Receivers are not required to check that the re-derived encryption_key...","description":"draft-ietf-mls-virtual-clients (virtual-clients-01), Creating LeafNodes and UpdatePaths. Editors' copy mlswg/mls-virtual-clients at 65e960d, L623.

Text: "When other emulator clients receive a LeafNode for the virtual client, they use
the `epoch_id` to determine the epoch of the emulation group from which to
derive the secrets necessary to re-create the key material of the LeafNode and
potential UpdatePath."

Problem: Receivers are not required to check that the re-derived encryption_key and UpdatePath public keys match the received ones. The draft also gives no behavior for an unknown epoch_id, a DerivationInfo decryption failure, a deleted generation or a mismatch. A faulty emulator client can therefore install a leaf whose private keys the other emulator clients silently get wrong.

Suggested fix: Require receivers to compare the re-derived public keys with the LeafNode and UpdatePath, and specify the action to take on each failure case.

Severity: medium. Verifier: narrow (Confirmed: L623-635 re-derives the key material but never requires comparing it with the received public keys, and L639-640 is the only reject rule. Open PR #30 adds only an epoch-ordering check. The proposed failure policy is a design choice, so the problem is narrowed to the missing check and the missing failure handling.)
